answer.generated: Linear superposition states that the total response of a neuron to multiple inputs is the sum of its responses to each individual input. In image processing, this principle allows a neural network to learn features locally, where each hidden unit receives connections from only a subset of pixels (sparse connectivity), yet still capture the combined effect of multiple stimuli. Additionally, parameter sharing ensures that the same weight parameters are used across all spatial positions, enabling the network to apply the same transformation consistently over the entire image while maintaining locality. Thus, linear superposition underpins both efficient local feature extraction and robust spatial invariance in deep learning architectures.
